TITLE: Proton-proton scattering at 98 and 142 MeV.
AUTHOR: (A.E.Taylor,E.Wood,L.Bird)
SAMPLE:
Two liquid hydrogen targets were used which had total
surface  densities of 1.31 and 1.11 g/cm2. The
evaporation rate from the target was about 10 cm3 of
liquid hydrogen per hour when most of the ortho-
parahydrogen conversion had taken place.
DETECTOR:
(TELES) A triple coincidence range telescope was used
to detect the scattered protons and the telescope
absorber was changed in order to maintain constant
efficiency of detection for the different scattering
angles. The counter telescope was mounted on an arm
which could be swung from side to side of the beam
direction and whose pivot was carefully set in the
centre of the collimated beam.
CORRECTION:
To obtain the true efficiency for any scattering
angle a small correction was added to the measured
value for those protons which were lost before being
detected by the telescope. This correction was
slightly energy sensitive amounting to 0.2% at 10 degr.
and 0.6% at 40 degrees for the 98 MeV determination.
ERR-ANALYS:
(DATA-ERR1) Absolute scale error
(DATA-ERR2) Total relative error
(ERR-1)  Counting errors
(ERR-2)  Uncertainty in measurement of the detector
efficiency
(ERR-3)  Possible deviation from an angle cosecant
dependence
(ERR-4)  Fluctuation in the ionization chamber
calibration
(ERR-5)  Uncertainty in the corrections applied to the
measured detector efficiency
(DATA-ERR3,3.,4.)The relative error between the
absolute scales of the separate determinations

FLAG:
(1.) Small angle telescope was used.
(2.) Large angle telescope was used.

TITLE:
A precision measurements of pp elastic scattering cross
sections at intermediate energies.
AUTHOR:
(D.Albers, F.Bauer, J.Bisplinghoff, R.Bollmann,
K.Buesser, M.Busch, R.Daniel, O.Diehl, F.Dohrmann,
H.P.Engelhardt, J.Ernst, P.D.Eversheim, M.Gasthuber,
R.Gebel, J.Greiff, A.Gross, R.Gross-Hardt, S.Heider,
A.Heine, F.Hinterberger, T.Hueskes, M.Igelbrink,
M.Jeske, R.Langkau, J.Lindlein, R.Maier, R.Maschuw,
F.Mosel, D.Prasuhn, H.Rohdjess, D.Rosendaal,
P.von Rossen, N.Scheid, N.Schirm, M.Schulz-Rojahn,
F.Schwandt, V.Schwarz, W.Scobel, S.Thomas,H.-J.Trelle,
E.Weise, A.Wellinghausen, K.Woller, R.Ziegler,
EDDA Collaboration)
REL-REF:
(R,C0083001,A.J.Simon+,J,PR/C,48,662,1993) The absolute
cross-section scale was fixed at the reference momentum
1.455 Gev/c to the high-precision data.
(R,,R.A.Arndt+,J,PR/C,50,2731,1994) Phase shift
solution SM94.
(R,,R.A.Arndt+,J,PR/C,56,3005,1997) Phase shift
solution SM97.
(R,,R.A.Arndt+,J,PR/C,62,34005,2000) Phase shift
solution FA00.
COMMENT:
-By authors. Including the data of the present work
will not only slightly modify the phase shifts to
reflect the differences to previous results but may
also allow to improve the ansatz for the variation of
the phase shift parameters with energy.
INSTITUTE:
(2GERBON) Helmholtz-Institute.
(2GERHAM) Institut fuer Experimentalphysik.
(2GERJUL) Institut fuer Kernphysik.
SAMPLE: Thin CH(2) fiber targets, thickness 5-mu-m, were used.
ADD-RES: (COMP) Phase shift solutions Sm94, Sm97, Fa00.
DETECTOR:
(SPEC) The EDDA detector. It consists of scintillator
bars and rings designed to measure the points, at which
the scattered proton and its recoil partner traverse
the hodoscope.  The kinematic relationship between
these angles are used to identify elastic scattering
events. Additional details see in original paper.
ERR-ANALYS:
(ERR-S).The errors that are uncorrelated for each
data point, this is given in the column statistical
this encompasses the purely statistical error from the
pp scattering yield, the error due to subtraction of
P-carbon scattering and errors introduced by angle-
reconstruction and cuts applied in the data analysis.
(ERR-1).The systematic errors which will be functions
smoothly varying with beam momentum and scattering
angle. This comprises the uncertainty on the overall
detection efficiency for pp elastic scattering and the
uncertainty on possible contaminations from pp-
inelastic  reactions.
(ERR-T).The total error is the quadratic sum of ERR-S
and ERR-1.
All data do not contain two types of normalization
uncertainties:  an overall normalization error of the
whole data set of less 1.5% due to the absolute
normalization at beam momentum 1455 MeV/c. There is an
Additional systematic uncertainty due to the relative
normalization of 2.5% common to all data points at the
same energy. This error does not apply at the
normalization point at 1455 MeV/c. The relative
normalization uncertainties at different beam momenta
are uncorrelated. This is a conservative upper limit
especially for beam momenta close to 1455 MeV/c.
